text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-delta-architecture/revised-b.md <<'EOF'
# Revised candidate: declaration IDs, complete evidence

Recommend changed-declaration acquisition followed by complete-snapshot interpretation. The correction removes member refreshes and automatic member backfills from this workflow. `MemberId` supplies an existing lookup and scope boundary; member metadata has its own separately scheduled lifecycle.

## Caller experience

```sh
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG
exposed data declarations sync --config CONFIG --resume RUN_ID
exposed data declarations reconcile --config CONFIG
```

Daily sync operates on a committed declaration cohort and evidence baseline. Initial capture and deliberate cohort expansion belong to declaration reconciliation, using already stored member IDs. Neither command fetches or loads member metadata. Missing prerequisites produce an actionable error. New stored members do not silently expand established historical coverage; report them as awaiting declaration onboarding. Retain former members already in scope.

## Alternatives and decision

1. Full declaration capture and content diff: simplest acquisition, greatest remote work.
2. Changed-member full histories: viable fallback, fewer merge cases but refetches unrelated declarations whenever one changes. It need not update member metadata, but is broader than the daily requirement.
3. Changed declaration IDs plus complete-snapshot resolution: recommended. Hydrate changed IDs, preserve all other evidence, and reuse global interpretation.
4. Fully incremental resolution: defer; requires durable identity components, reverse dependencies, alias retention, and explicit identity merge/split rules.

The existing pipeline already interprets complete evidence globally. Incremental acquisition is a useful boundary without redesigning identity semantics.

## Acquisition contract

Freeze an inclusive source-date window with overlap and indexing lag. Union publication-filtered and update-filtered discovery results. Treat these payloads exclusively as ID discovery: observed filtered versions are truncated. Fetch each discovered ID unfiltered, including expired records and retaining all returned versions and source JSON. Registration dates are not correction timestamps.

Discovery may return records outside the cohort. Record their IDs, owners, and exclusion reason in the run receipt; they are explicitly outside coverage. For in-scope records, missing lookups, ownership conflicts, failed hydration, inconsistent pagination, and missing required parent evidence fail sealing. Never classify an error as an exclusion. Unknown ownership cannot be excluded until established. No member metadata retrieval is a recovery action.

Merge hydrated records into the complete immutable declaration-ID snapshot, indexed by owner and parent reference. Hydrate missing same-member parent declarations recursively, with cycle/conflict detection; preserve known parent evidence even when absent from discovery. Existing complete evidence remains available for unchanged children and global funder resolution. An omitted record or version is a discrepancy, never deletion evidence. Retain prior evidence pending an explicit source-supported retirement policy; conflicting versions require a documented selection rule, not arrival order.

Seal only after all required requests and dependency checks succeed. Manifest hashes, capture times, scope, query policy, base revision, and receipts make reused evidence distinguishable from fresh observations.

## Types and ownership

```rust
struct DeclarationCohort { /* explicit retained MemberIds */ }
struct DiscoveryWindow { /* checked source dates */ }
struct CompleteDeclarationSnapshot { /* verified records and dependencies */ }
struct PreparedPublication { /* run, expected revision, artifacts */ }
enum ScopeDecision { Included(MemberId), Excluded(ExclusionReason) }
enum PublishOutcome { Committed, AlreadyCommitted, StaleBase }

async fn synchronize(&self) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
async fn resume(&self, run: IngestionKey) -> Result<SyncReport, EntityIngestionError>;
async fn hydrate(&self, ids: DeclarationIds) -> Result<HydratedDeclarations, SourceError>;
```

Domain types own scope and completeness. The service orchestrates; Parliament parses external records; artifact storage owns durable snapshots; the existing loader owns transactional publication.

Run global clean/resolve and publish complete resolved evidence, retaining parent and alias context. Atomically commit projection, groups, artifact reference, and checkpoint under the existing loader lock with expected-revision protection. Check already-committed runs first. Empty successful scans advance revision and coverage without identity churn.

## Risks

Discovery is not a documented lossless changefeed; overlap and periodic declaration reconciliation mitigate omissions. Global resolution still costs work, and ingestion-derived noncompany IDs may change. Durable raw evidence remains essential. Verify baseline-plus-delta equivalence, parent-only corrections, out-of-scope receipts, in-scope failures, restart, and competing publication before rollout.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));
